title: The Adventure Begins
logline: When Keen leaves home with his father’s empty wristbands, a storm at sea and a trapped dolphin teach him that real courage is not looking fearless — it is hearing the gulp and diving in anyway.

episodeVision.premise: Keen sets out from home to find Crystal Cove, carrying his late father’s vacant wristbands and a brave face that is not yet the same as courage. A storm strips away the performance, and saving Squeaky reveals the courage already inside him before Aida welcomes him into the Crystal Bears.
episodeVision.dramaticQuestion: Can Keen stop pretending to be fearless long enough to act through the fear — and can the world meet that act as belonging rather than proof he must stand alone?
episodeVision.theme: Courage is not the absence of fear; courage is the step, the dive, or the promise made while the fear is still present.
episodeVision.externalJourney: A warm morning departure becomes a solo sail, then a storm, then a rescue, then arrival at Crystal Cove, crystal-award ceremony and first found-family walk along the beach.
episodeVision.internalJourney: Keen begins performing readiness for his Mum and himself. He loses the map, loses the boat, and nearly loses Squeaky; in the underwater nadir he stops posturing and anchors himself in the wristbands’ meaning. By the end he can receive welcome without needing to prove he belongs.
episodeVision.relationshipChanges: Keen and his Mum shift from protected child and holding parent into trusted traveler and the home that goes with him. Keen and Squeaky become rescue-bonded friends. Aida moves from distant witness to welcomer. The bears move from strangers on the shore to family around him. Fuzzby turns Keen into an instant legend, while Zenny keeps the welcome gentle enough to breathe.
episodeVision.emotionalCurve: Playful pollen comedy opens the world, then Aida’s still knowing gives the story gravity. The pier goodbye is warm and aching. The ocean begins comic and exploratory before fear tightens into storm. The underwater rescue is the darkest point, held on effort and breath. Connection returns through beacon, rescue, welcome and crystal ceremony, ending with laughter that still remembers the storm and Mum left behind.
episodeVision.comedyCurve: Fuzzby’s proud-bumbler pollen sequence supplies big physical laughs before the storm warning. Keen’s map confidence and boat wobble mirror Fuzzby’s cover-up comedy in a more tender register. Fuzzby’s emergency arrival turns panic into slapstick without deflating stakes. After the rescue, Fuzzby’s instant hero-worship and honey-friendship agenda release the episode’s held tension.
episodeVision.setupPayoffMap: Fuzzby’s 'Nailed it' cover-up sets the comic grammar that Keen later echoes with his boat wobble. The distant thunder in the flower field pays off as the storm at sea. Aida’s vision plants the pier and the goodbye before we live it. Keen’s repeated checking exposes the brave-face mask before the wristbands are given. The vacant wristbands are handed over with no glow, then faintly self-glow underwater, then receive the Aquamarine gems in the ceremony. Mum’s promise that Keen will never be alone is echoed by Aida as found-family truth. Squeaky’s playful arrival pays off as the friend whose need calls Keen’s courage out.
episodeVision.visualMotifs: Open flowers and pollen at bee scale; empty gold wristbands; hands closing and opening; a small boat against wide water; maps turning useless; storm-grey swallowing the horizon; a single aqua glow underwater; a crystal beacon cutting rain; wet sand and rain droplets after the storm; the final group walking as one along a golden beach.
episodeVision.sonicMotifs: Fuzzby’s manic buzz-crash rhythm against Zenny’s stillness; Aida’s low crystal bowl tone; Mum’s quiet pauses at the pier; Squeaky’s chirps shifting from play to distress to relief; wind growing into storm; muffled underwater sound around Keen’s breath; the faint B-note courage shimmer from the wristbands; the bears’ combined call becoming a beacon chord; golden-hour surf under final laughter.
episodeVision.climax: Keen dives into storm water without hesitation, fights the net around Squeaky while running out of strength, sees the vacant wristbands glow from within, braces against the submerged rock, tears the net free and survives the wave with Squeaky’s help.
episodeVision.resolution: Aida awards Keen the Aquamarine crystal, which splits into two gems and settles into his father’s wristbands. The bears hug him into belonging, and the episode ends with the new family walking the beach while Fuzzby enthusiastically plans a honey-based friendship.
episodeVision.intendedFinalFeeling: Warm, buoyant belonging with a trace of ache: Keen is home in a new place, but the image still carries the storm, the lost boat, and the Mum who had to let him go.

orderedEvents.text: Tall flowers sway gently in the warm breeze. Some stretch high above the grass, with long soft necks and bright open petals full of pollen. FUZZBY and ZENNY weave between them collecting pollen from flower to flower. Tiny pollen sacks bounce on their back legs. Zenny works with smooth calm precision — neat, efficient, graceful. Fuzzby does not. He zig-zags wildly through the air, humming loudly to himself as he works.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: BIZZY-BIZZY-BIZZY, BIZZY-BIZZY-BIZZY…
He dips low into a flower, scoops up pollen — then overdoes it and spins sideways into a leaf. FWIP. He bounces back into the air and straightens up proudly.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: Nailed it.
Zenny glides up beside him. Watches him for a beat.

beats.storyBeat: At bee height in the sunlit flower field, Zenny’s precise work and Fuzzby’s chaotic overconfidence define the comic relationship instantly. Fuzzby wants pollen-gathering to look effortless; the leaf rebound exposes that his body is already arguing with his self-image.
beats.want: Fuzzby wants to look like a master pollen professional while Zenny witnesses him.
beats.need: He needs to learn that being wanted is not the same as being flawless; the messy truth is part of why Zenny stays near him.
beats.kidRead: A silly bee zooms too fast, bonks a leaf, and acts proud anyway.
beats.adultRead: It is the tiny workplace comedy of someone covering embarrassment before anyone can name it, with a partner who sees the whole truth.
beats.emotionalIntent: Open with laughter, momentum and character contrast: Fuzzby as motion, Zenny as control, affection hiding under irritation.
